findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] with no nil guard, so it raises NoMethodError whenever the embed_category row is absent from site_settings — the normal state, since Discourse persists only explicitly-changed settings — making the 'if category_id == 0' uncategorized fallback unreachable dead code. rake db:migrate aborts with "undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass" on every fresh install (site_settings is empty at migrate time, seeding runs later) and on every existing site whose admin never saved embed_category, blocking all deploys and CI at this commit; the author's own sibling guard (cmd_tuples > 0 before embeddable_hosts[0]) proves [0] returns nil on empty results.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim without stripping protocol or path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches lower(host) = URI(referer).host, so migrated rows like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' — formats the removed specs show the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported — can never match any referer. Sites upgrading with URL-formatted host entries silently lose embedding immediately after the migration: every embedded-comments request raises Discourse::InvalidAccess until an admin hand-fixes each broken row in the new UI.

[BUG] The host validation regex caps TLDs at {2,5} characters and requires at least one dot, rejecting valid hostnames such as 'forum.example.museum' (or .travel/.online) and single-label hosts like 'localhost' that the previous free-text setting accepted. Admins on long-gTLD or dot-less intranet hosts get a validation error and can never register their embedding host, leaving the embedding feature permanently broken for those domains with no workaround.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host runs where("lower(host) = ?") on every embed request, replacing the previous in-memory-cached SiteSetting comparison, and the migration creates no index on the host column. Every reader of every page embedding Discourse comments now costs an extra DB roundtrip (plus an unindexed scan) on the hottest anonymous path, so high-traffic embedding sites take a per-request DB load increase at deploy time.

[BUG] The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard, so saving a record with a nil host attribute raises NoMethodError before validation ever runs. A POST/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts whose embeddable_host payload omits the host key returns a 500 (NoMethodError on nil.sub!) instead of the 4xx validation error that render_json_error is there to produce.

[BUG] update and destroy pass the fetched record straight to save_host/host.destroy without checking it exists. A PUT or DELETE against an already-deleted id — e.g. a second admin removing the same row from a stale tab — raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404.

[BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] without verifying the embeddable_host key is present. A POST/PUT with an empty or malformed body crashes with NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx error response.

[BUG] The INSERT statement string-interpolates the legacy host value ('#{h}') into raw SQL with no quoting, so any stored entry containing a single quote aborts the migration. A site whose admin saved a host value containing an apostrophe cannot complete the upgrade — db:migrate crashes with a SQL syntax error at this INSERT.

[ADVISORY] The two fabricator files' contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while every category fabricator (:diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Both files still load so the suite passes, but any maintainer opening category_fabricator.rb by name to change category fixtures finds no category fabricators there, and blame/git-history for the category fabricators now points at a brand-new unrelated file.

[ADVISORY] update discards all submitted parameters and re-serializes a freshly-fetched OpenStruct (fetch_embedding rebuilds it from the DB every request), so PUT /admin/customize/embedding always returns 200 while persisting nothing. Any API client that PUTs embedding changes receives a success response with the unchanged payload — a silent no-op public endpoint the diff explicitly registers a route for.

[ADVISORY] The saveChanges action is unreachable — no template in the diff wires it — and its body sends an empty payload (update({})) to the no-op update endpoint. A future maintainer wiring a save button inherits a stub that submits no data to a controller that ignores it anyway, and reviewers reading the controller are misled into believing an embedding-settings save flow exists.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new controller asserts class ancestry; create, update, destroy, and save_host's blank-category-to-uncategorized fallback have no behavioral coverage, and the embedding controller spec is equally hollow. The nil-record and nil-params 500s and a regression in the uncategorized_category_id fallback all pass CI because nothing in the diff exercises save_host or the destroy path.

[ADVISORY] SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? and the embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings are deleted outright with no deprecation cycle, so out-of-tree code referencing them raises NoMethodError after upgrade. Plugins or admin tooling that read the public embeddable_hosts setting crash at runtime on upgrade (SiteSetting raises for unknown setting names) instead of seeing a deprecation warning.

[BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] with no nil guard, so db:migrate raises NoMethodError (undefined method [] for nil) on any install whose embed_category site_settings row is absent — the default state, since Discourse only persists changed settings, as the author's own cmd_tuples > 0 guard for embeddable_hosts three lines below acknowledges — or whose stored value matches no category name; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable dead code because an empty result yields nil, never a zero-id hash. Sites that never configured embedding (the majority, as embedding is opt-in) or that renamed/deleted the configured category hit nil['id'] and the migration aborts, blocking the upgrade/deploy for every such install.

[BUG] The back-compat data migration inserts each legacy embeddable_hosts value verbatim via interpolated SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping http(s):// (e.g. 'http://discourse.org', a form the old spec 'works with a http host' proved supported) are stored with the scheme intact and never match record_for_host's where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) comparison, which only ever sees a bare hostname. Embeds from every scheme-prefixed allowlisted host raise Discourse::InvalidAccess immediately after upgrade while the rows look intact in the new admin table, and the migration's final DELETE (line 31) destroys the original setting values, leaving nothing to recover the configuration from; the specs mask this because Fabricate saves the same legacy-form values through the model's normalization.

[BUG] update and destroy both fetch EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and dereference the result without a nil check, so save_host(nil) executes host.host = ... and destroy executes host.destroy on nil. A request targeting a nonexistent or already-deleted embeddable_host id (stale admin tab after a concurrent delete, or any direct API call) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 where the CRUD contract expects a 404, polluting error logs and breaking the client's error handling.

[BUG] The new validates_format_of regex explicitly endorses an optional (:[0-9]{1,5})? port, but before_validation strips only the scheme and path while record_for_host matches against URI#host, which never contains a port, so a host like 'example.com:3000' passes validation and is persisted but is guaranteed to fail every embed-authorization lookup. The admin UI accepts and saves a host that raises 'invalid referer host' for every embed attempt from that origin, with no validation or UI feedback indicating the saved configuration is unmatchable by the enforcement path.

[ADVISORY] The same validation regex requires a dot and caps the TLD at five letters (\.[a-z]{2,5}), rejecting dotless hostnames and long TLDs (localhost, site.museum, blog.travel) that the previous free-text embeddable_hosts setting accepted and matched. A migrated row holding such a legacy value is displayed in the admin table but any edit-and-save of it fails the new format validation, so an admin who previously embedded from 'localhost' (dev setups) or a >5-letter TLD cannot re-save that host through the new UI at all.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation and the migration creates no unique index on host, while record_for_host resolves duplicate rows via where(...).first, so the same hostname can be stored twice with different category_id values and the lookup silently picks the lowest-id row. An admin who adds the same host twice with different categories (nothing client- or server-side prevents it) gets every embedded topic for that host created in the older row's category regardless of the newer entry's intent, and nothing flags the conflicting configuration.

[ADVISORY] belongs_to :category has no presence validation and nothing re-points or nullifies embeddable_hosts.category_id when a category is deleted — Discourse's category-deletion flow remaps topics but knows nothing about this new table, and there is no dependent option or destroy/reassign hook. Deleting a category that an allowlisted host references leaves a dangling category_id row; the next TopicEmbed.import for that host passes a nonexistent category to PostCreator and topic creation for that host fails with no surfaced error, silently killing feed embedding for that host.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddingController#update persists nothing — it only re-renders the same OpenStruct built by fetch_embedding — and the client saveChanges action that calls embedding.update({}) is wired to no element in embedding.hbs, making the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route, the update action, and the client action inert dead code (the deletion test passes: removing the route in config/routes.rb, this action, and saveChanges removes the lying contract entirely). The shipped update route accepts and silently discards any payload, so a future developer who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action ships silent data loss believing the endpoint persists settings.

[ADVISORY] The only spec added for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance (verified: this file's single it-block checks Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController and no other spec in the diff references this controller), leaving the controller's entire behavior surface unverified — the blank-category_id-to-uncategorized defaulting, the render_json_error path for invalid hosts, and create/update/destroy request handling have zero assertions. A regression in the uncategorized fallback (e.g. dropping host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if blank?) breaks every host saved without a category and every embed-import's category assignment, and the build stays green because no test exercises the controller's actual behavior.

[ADVISORY] The embedding controller spec likewise asserts only inheritance, so the load-path contract the new admin page depends on — EmbeddingSerializer emitting embeddable_host_ids plus an embeddable_hosts side-load array that the store's new plural _hydrateEmbedded branch consumes — is verified by no server spec anywhere in the diff (only the generic fruit/color fixtures in store-test exercise the hydration). Changing the association name or dropping embed: :ids fails no spec while the admin embedding page renders with unhydrated host rows and a broken table at runtime; the feature's core load path is guarded only by an unrelated fixture.

[ADVISORY] The new component's non-trivial state logic — buffered save with props.category_id assembly, rollbackBuffer on cancel, the isNew-vs-persisted cancel branch, and categoryId initialization on edit — is exercised by no JavaScript test in the diff even though this PR extends the existing qunit suite (store-test, create-pretender). A regression in the save/cancel path — e.g. cancel on a new host no longer removing it from embedding.embeddable_hosts, or edit no longer seeding categoryId so save resets the category to uncategorized — ships completely undetected, biting admins on the next change to this component.

[ADVISORY] The final content of category_fabricator.rb is only the new embeddable_host fabricator while all four pre-existing category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) now live in spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the two files' contents are swapped relative to their names. The next contributor grepping for or editing the :category fabricator lands on the wrong file, git blame/history for the category fabricators is misdirected to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and any 'cleanup' that re-homes the definitions creates conflicting duplicate Fabricator registrations.

[BUG] The migration reads site_settings rows with no guard for absence, so `execute(...WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'...)[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError on nil whenever no embed_category site_settings row exists — every fresh install and every site that never overrode that setting — aborting db:migrate before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can ever run. Fresh installs and all sites that never set embed_category fail db:migrate at this migration, blocking every upgrade containing this commit until the SQL is patched by hand.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim into the new table while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches `lower(host)` against the bare parsed hostname, so legacy entries stored as 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — forms the old feature's own specs explicitly supported — never match after the upgrade (the model's stripping only runs on save, and the migration bypasses the model). Upgraded sites whose admins entered scheme- or path-qualified hosts get 'invalid referer host' Discourse::InvalidAccess on every embedded comment page and rejected feed imports, silently, until an admin re-saves each row in the new UI.

[BUG] update feeds `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` — nil for a nonexistent id — straight into save_host, which executes `host.host = ...` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Saving an edit against a host another admin has just deleted (stale list) returns a 500 instead of a 404, showing the admin a server-error popup with no recovery path.

[BUG] destroy calls `host.destroy` on the result of `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check, raising NoMethodError when the id no longer exists. Two admins deleting the same host makes the second DELETE return a 500 instead of a 404, and because the component's `destroyRecord().then()` has no rejection handler the row silently stays in the admin list looking undeleted.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update renders the serialized embedding without applying any request params — the OpenStruct embedding has no editable fields — and no template in the diff invokes the frontend saveChanges action, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and the admin-embedding.js saveChanges/update({}) path are implementation work traceable to no requirement. Any client that PUTs /admin/customize/embedding receives a 200 success for a request that persisted nothing, and a future contributor who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action ships a control that silently does nothing.

[ADVISORY] The per-request embed allow-list check changed from the in-memory cached SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, which runs an uncached `WHERE lower(host) = ?` query on every embed request, and the migration creates no index on host. Every embedded page's /embed/comments hit now costs a DB round trip (a scan, since a plain index would not serve lower()) — high-embed-traffic sites lose the previous zero-DB allow-list path and gain load proportional to embed views.

[ADVISORY] before_validation strips the scheme and path but not the port while the format regex explicitly accepts `:[0-9]{1,5}`, and record_for_host compares the stored value against `uri.host` with the port removed, so a port-qualified host that validation and the UI accept can never match a referer. An admin who saves 'staging.example.com:8080' (accepted by the validation the diff itself added) gets 'invalid referer host' InvalidAccess for every embed from that origin, with the stored row permanently unmatchable until hand-edited.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost enforces only host format with no uniqueness validation and no unique index, while record_for_host resolves duplicates via `.first`, so two rows for the same host are accepted — including case variants, since the format regex is case-insensitive and the lookup lowercases. An admin who adds a case-variant duplicate and edits its category sees the edit accepted while embedded topics keep posting to the first row's category, with nothing indicating the edited row is dead.

[ADVISORY] The new belongs_to :category relationship registers no cleanup anywhere in the diff, so deleting a category that an embeddable host references leaves embeddable_hosts.category_id dangling. After an admin deletes a used category, TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator under skip_validations: true and creates topics pointing at a nonexistent category, and the admin UI renders that host row with a blank category via Discourse.Category.findById.

[ADVISORY] category_fabricator.rb was emptied of every category fabricator and now defines the :embeddable_host fabricator, with the category definitions moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the two files' contents are swapped relative to their names. The next contributor editing category fabrication opens category_fabricator.rb and finds the embedding fabricator instead, and a later cleanup that re-homes each fabricator to its matching filename creates duplicate Fabricator definitions where load order silently picks a winner.

[ADVISORY] The new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains only the category fabricators removed from category_fabricator.rb, while the actual :embeddable_host fabricator was written into category_fabricator.rb. Anyone hunting the definition of :embeddable_host is sent to the wrong file, and a future reorganization that adds it to this correctly-named file produces two competing definitions resolved only by file load order.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts ancestry; none of the diff's new behavior — save_host's create/update, the blank-category_id default to uncategorized, render_json_error, or not-found handling — is exercised by any test in the diff. The nil-on-missing-id 500s and any payload/param-name mismatch between the frontend save props and `params[:embeddable_host]` ship undetected and surface only as a broken embedding admin page in production.

[ADVISORY] The embedding controller spec asserts only ancestry, and no test in the diff covers Admin::EmbeddingController#show's serialization — the embeddable_host_ids side-load feeding the store's new plural hydration that the entire embedding admin page depends on. A payload-shape regression (embed: :ids emitting a key the new _hydrateEmbedded branch mishandles) renders the admin embedding page permanently empty with no failing test anywhere.

[BUG] The migration copies legacy embeddable_hosts values into embeddable_hosts.host verbatim via raw SQL INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so legacy entries stored with a scheme and/or path (e.g. 'http://discourse.org', 'https://example.com/1234' — formats the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported via URI(h).host, as asserted by the old specs) can never match record_for_host's lookup lower(host) = uri.host. On every pre-existing install that configured hosts with a scheme or path, all embed requests start returning 403 'invalid referer host' immediately after upgrade with zero signal in the new admin UI (the rows still display and look configured), and re-saving such a row fails the new format validation until the admin retypes the host from scratch — the embed comments feature is silently broken site-wide.

[BUG] The validation regex explicitly permits an optional :port and the before_validation normalization strips only the scheme and path (never the port), but record_for_host matches against URI#host which excludes the port, so a host saved as e.g. 'localhost:3000' or 'intranet.corp:8080' can never match any referer. An admin can enter a port-suffixed host that both the regex and the UI accept, the row saves and displays normally, and every embed request from that origin is then rejected with 403 'invalid referer host' — the configuration is accepted by the write path but is unmatchable by the read path, so the admin has no way to discover why embedding fails.

[BUG] The create_table adds no unique index on host and the model adds no uniqueness validation (and the format regex's /i flag means case-variants like 'Evil.com' and 'evil.com' are both storable), so duplicate host rows with conflicting category_id values are representable, while record_for_host selects with an unordered where(...).first. An admin can add the same host twice with two different categories (nothing blocks the second save), and which record — and therefore which category TopicEmbed.import assigns to newly embedded topics — is decided by arbitrary database row order; deleting one of the duplicates does not visibly change which category wins, so topics land in an unpredictable category.

[BUG] Nothing maintains referential integrity for embeddable_hosts.category_id (no FK, no dependent-cleanup on category deletion), and the edit() action derives categoryId from the client-resolved host.category.id — so when the host's category cannot be resolved client-side (deleted after page load, dangling id), categoryId becomes undefined, jQuery serializes it as an empty string, and save() sends a blank category_id that the controller's blank? fallback silently converts to Uncategorized. Deleting a category that embeddable hosts still reference leaves dangling rows; the next time an admin edits such a host (even just to fix a typo), its category is silently reassigned to Uncategorized and all subsequently embedded topics from that host start landing in Uncategorized instead of the intended category — and until then TopicEmbed.import passes the nonexistent category_id to PostCreator, failing imports for that host.

[BUG] where("lower(host) = ?", host) lowercases only the stored column and not the parsed referer/embed-URL host, so the intended case-insensitive match is only half-implemented and a DNS-legitimate mixed-case referer like http://EvilTrout.com/ never matches the configured host. A site configured for a host receives embed requests whose referer carries any uppercase letters in the hostname and gets a 403 'invalid referer host' for a host that is demonstrably in the allowed list — the admin sees the host configured but embedding fails depending purely on client-side casing.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing — it renders the exact same serializer payload as #show — so PUT /admin/customize/embedding is an advertised route that discards its entire request body and returns 200, and the client's wired saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6) calls this no-op. Any consumer that PUTs embedding data gets a success response while every field is silently dropped; the next developer who wires the existing saveChanges action to a save button ships a UI that tells admins their changes saved while persisting nothing.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance and exercises none of the controller's new behavior — save_host's parameter handling, the blank→uncategorized_category_id fallback, render_json_error, or destroy — so the entire new logic ships as a stand-in guard. CI stays green through any regression in save_host (a dropped blank? fallback, a renamed params key, a broken error path), so the next refactor silently ships 500s or wrongly-categorized hosts to production admins with a green build.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new Admin::EmbeddingController asserts class inheritance and never exercises the show/update serialization path (including the embed: :ids side-loading the new store hydration depends on), so the endpoint's contract is entirely untested. A regression in EmbeddingSerializer's embeddable_host_ids emission or the OpenStruct payload shape breaks the whole admin embedding page (empty host table) while this spec and the build stay green.

[ADVISORY] The new plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded deletes the raw *_ids key unconditionally and its hydrated || [] fallback is dead code (Array#map always returns a truthy array), so any id whose _lookupSubType fails is silently replaced by an undefined entry in the hydrated array and the original ids are destroyed — unlike the singular branch, which retains the raw *_id key when hydration fails. This is shared store infrastructure, not embedding-specific: any future payload using a foo_ids key with an unresolvable id (partial side-load, id absent from the client's category list) gets a broken array containing undefined where consumers iterate records (rendering crashes on undefined.host) and permanently loses the raw ids the old code preserved; the author's intended failure fallback never runs.

[ADVISORY] The diff swaps file contents: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all four suite-wide category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, so file name and contents contradict each other. Maintainers hunting for the category fabricator definitions every spec file depends on find an embeddable_host fabricator in the category file instead; anyone who 'fixes' this by recreating category_fabricator.rb with the category definitions silently redefines Fabricator(:category) in a second file, making resolution depend on load order.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) replaces the previously in-process-cached SiteSetting read with an uncached database query (WHERE lower(host) = ?, which no existing index supports — the migration creates none, and a plain b-tree on host would not even serve the lower() predicate) executed on every single embed comments request. Every page view on every embedding site now adds a sequential-scan query per request on a hot path the old code served from memory with zero database round-trips; high-traffic embedding hosts multiply database load, and the load is invisible until N grows.

[BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup without checking for an empty result, so it raises NoMethodError on nil whenever no site_settings row named 'embed_category' exists, and the uncategorized_category_id fallback on line 15 repeats the same unguarded [0] access. db:migrate aborts during deploy for every fresh install and every site that never overrode embed_category (setting defaults are not materialized as site_settings rows), rolling back the new table and blocking the release; the guarded cmd_tuples check on the embeddable_hosts query three lines below shows the empty-result case was anticipated there but not here.

[BUG] The migration's raw INSERT copies legacy embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, applying neither the model's scheme/path normalization (which Fabricate-based specs prove runs on every normal save) nor any SQL escaping. A legacy entry like 'http://eviltrout.com' — which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping the scheme — is stored as-is and can never satisfy record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison, so those sites' embedded comments start failing with 'invalid referer host' after the upgrade until an admin manually re-saves each host; additionally a legacy value containing a single quote aborts the migration with a SQL syntax error.

[BUG] update and destroy dereference the record returned by EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first without a nil check, and save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without verifying the envelope exists. A PUT or DELETE for a host id that no longer exists (deleted from another admin tab or session) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404/JSON error, and any request missing the embeddable_host param envelope 500s the same way; the frontend destroy action has no .catch on destroyRecord, so the user sees the row silently stay in the table.

[BUG] The validates_format_of regex is inconsistent both with the hosts the old embeddable_hosts setting accepted and with record_for_host's exact match: it rejects 'localhost', IP addresses, and TLDs longer than 5 characters, while accepting port-suffixed hosts that before_validation does not strip. Admins with local or intranet embed targets can no longer whitelist them at all, and a legacy 'localhost' row inserted verbatim by the migration still matches embeds but fails validation on every edit, so its category cannot be changed — the exact capability this PR advertises — leaving deletion as the only operation; conversely 'example.com:8080' saves successfully yet lower(host) = uri.host can never authorize it, producing a silently dead allowlist entry.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import now derives the post's category solely from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) (eh.try(:category_id)), so an import whose URL matches no whitelisted host posts to Uncategorized, while the migration deletes the embed_category setting that previously routed such imports. Admins who use the retained feed_polling_* features with a feed URL whose host is not an embeddable host — or with no hosts configured at all — find every newly imported RSS/ATOM topic in Uncategorized after the upgrade, with the setting that used to control this destroyed and no replacement anywhere in the new UI.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update discards the request payload entirely and re-renders the current state, making PUT /admin/customize/embedding a persistence no-op that returns success. The admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action is wired to this endpoint, so any future settings UI or API client that PUTs embedding attributes receives a 200 while nothing is saved — an inert endpoint that should either accept attributes or not be routed.

[ADVISORY] The diff swaps two fabricator files' contents: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all four category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Specs still pass because Fabricator registration is global, but the next maintainer who deletes or renames 'the embeddable host fabricator file' removes every category fabricator and breaks the whole suite, and anyone editing category fabricators is sent to the wrong file — the blob hash a37f5b4c8ba moving from category_fabricator.rb to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb proves this is an accidental swap, not a refactor.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts it is a subclass of AdminController, leaving create/update/destroy request behavior completely untested. save_host's blank-category defaulting to uncategorized, the validation-error JSON path, and the 'embeddable_host' serializer root that the Ember save flow depends on have no coverage, so a server-contract regression in the admin embedding page — including the nil-id and missing-param 500s — passes CI and is discovered only as a broken admin UI.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table is created with no unique index on host, and the controller performs no duplicate-host check. An admin (or a legacy newline list containing a repeated host, which migrates verbatim into duplicate rows) can create two rows for the same host with different categories, after which record_for_host's unordered where().first routes each new embedded topic to an arbitrary one of the two categories — nondeterministic category assignment that is very hard to debug.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new Admin::EmbeddingController asserts subclass-ness, leaving the show serialization contract — root 'embedding' with embeddable_host_ids plus the side-loaded records that the new store plural-ids hydration consumes — untested. A regression in EmbeddingSerializer's embed: :ids output or in store.js's newly added _ids hydration branch silently renders the entire admin embedding page as an empty host table, with no failing spec anywhere in this diff to catch it.

[BUG] The migration interpolates each legacy embeddable_hosts setting line directly into an unescaped SQL string (execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"), so a single quote in any stored host line breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL during migration. An operator upgrading a site whose embeddable_hosts value contains a quote character — whether from a past admin entry, a site import, or a restored backup — has attacker-influenced SQL executed with full database privileges at deploy time; even a benign apostrophe aborts the migration and blocks the upgrade for the whole instance.

[BUG] The migration copies each legacy embeddable_hosts setting line verbatim into the host column without the model's scheme/path stripping, while the new record_for_host requires an exact lower(host) = URI(...).host match, so migrated entries like 'https://example.com/1234' — a form the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported by URI-parsing each line — can never match after the upgrade. Operators whose embeddable_hosts contained scheme- or path-prefixed entries (exactly the 'https://example.com/1234' form the old code and its specs supported) silently lose those allowed hosts: every embed and topic-retriever request from them raises Discourse::InvalidAccess after upgrade, breaking the embedded comment sections on those external sites with no migration-time warning.

[BUG] update feeds EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first — nil for any nonexistent or already-deleted id — straight into save_host, whose `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404. adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds an INSERT via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from the legacy `site_settings` value and is not escaped/quoted safely, any host containing a single quote will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration (and it also creates an injection risk within the migration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update discards all submitted parameters and re-serializes a freshly-fetched OpenStruct (fetch_embedding rebuilds it from the DB every request), so PUT /admin/customize/embedding always returns 200 while persisting nothing. Any API client that PUTs embedding changes receives a success response with the unchanged payload — a silent no-op public endpoint the diff explicitly registers a route for.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, the `update` action ignores all request params and simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`. Since `@embedding` is always rebuilt in `fetch_embedding` as a new `OpenStruct` from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` cannot persist any changes and will always return a successful serialized payload reflecting current DB state. The diff also explicitly registers this PUT route (`config/routes.rb`), so the endpoint’s update semantics are a silent no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The saveChanges action is unreachable — no template in the diff wires it — and its body sends an empty payload (update({})) to the no-op update endpoint. A future maintainer wiring a save button inherits a stub that submits no data to a controller that ignores it anyway, and reviewers reading the controller are misled into believing an embedding-settings save flow exists.

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember controller `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload. In the new template `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`, there is no button or UI element invoking `saveChanges` (only `addHost` is wired via `{{d-button ... action="addHost"}}`, and per-host actions are in the `embeddable-host` component). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op that just re-renders the serializer without persisting anything. This is not a current functional defect (since nothing calls it), but it is dead/stubbed flow that can mislead maintainers/reviewers into thinking a settings save path exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec for the new controller asserts class ancestry; create, update, destroy, and save_host's blank-category-to-uncategorized fallback have no behavioral coverage, and the embedding controller spec is equally hollow. The nil-record and nil-params 500s and a regression in the uncategorized_category_id fallback all pass CI because nothing in the diff exercises save_host or the destroy path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces real 500-risk paths in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`: both `update` and `destroy` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb). If the id is missing/invalid, `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`), likewise `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, causing exceptions. Additionally, `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` exists (`params[:embeddable_host][:host]`), so malformed requests will also raise. The new controller specs indeed only assert ancestry and do not exercise these behaviors, so CI wouldn’t catch these regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? and the embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings are deleted outright with no deprecation cycle, so out-of-tree code referencing them raises NoMethodError after upgrade. Plugins or admin tooling that read the public embeddable_hosts setting crash at runtime on upgrade (SiteSetting raises for unknown setting names) instead of seeing a deprecation warning.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the public API surface `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` (deleted from `app/models/site_setting.rb`) and removes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings (deleted from `config/site_settings.yml`, locale entries removed, and the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` deletes those rows from `site_settings`). While core code is updated to use `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` and per-host categories, this is a backward-compatibility break for any out-of-tree code/plugins that still call `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` or read `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`/`SiteSetting.embed_category`, which would now raise errors after upgrade. The diff shows no deprecation shim or transitional alias.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] with no nil guard, so db:migrate raises NoMethodError (undefined method [] for nil) on any install whose embed_category site_settings row is absent — the default state, since Discourse only persists changed settings, as the author's own cmd_tuples > 0 guard for embeddable_hosts three lines below acknowledges — or whose stored value matches no category name; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable dead code because an empty result yields nil, never a zero-id hash. Sites that never configured embedding (the majority, as embedding is opt-in) or that renamed/deleted the configured category hit nil['id'] and the migration aborts, blocking the upgrade/deploy for every such install.
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same core bug: the migration indexes into the first row of execute(...) without verifying a row exists, leading to a crash (nil/empty result) when the embed_category site_setting is absent or doesn’t match a category, which can break upgrades and the related embedding/category-host feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The back-compat data migration inserts each legacy embeddable_hosts value verbatim via interpolated SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping http(s):// (e.g. 'http://discourse.org', a form the old spec 'works with a http host' proved supported) are stored with the scheme intact and never match record_for_host's where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) comparison, which only ever sees a bare hostname. Embeds from every scheme-prefixed allowlisted host raise Discourse::InvalidAccess immediately after upgrade while the rows look intact in the new admin table, and the migration's final DELETE (line 31) destroys the original setting values, leaving nothing to recover the configuration from; the specs mask this because Fabricate saves the same legacy-form values through the model's normalization.

[BUG] update and destroy both fetch EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and dereference the result without a nil check, so save_host(nil) executes host.host = ... and destroy executes host.destroy on nil. A request targeting a nonexistent or already-deleted embeddable_host id (stale admin tab after a concurrent delete, or any direct API call) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 where the CRUD contract expects a 404, polluting error logs and breaking the client's error handling.
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that update/destroy retrieve EmbeddableHost by id with `.where(...).first` and then call methods on the result without checking for nil, causing NoMethodError when the record doesn’t exist—exactly the golden issue (and adds expected 404 vs 500 impact).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new validates_format_of regex explicitly endorses an optional (:[0-9]{1,5})? port, but before_validation strips only the scheme and path while record_for_host matches against URI#host, which never contains a port, so a host like 'example.com:3000' passes validation and is persisted but is guaranteed to fail every embed-authorization lookup. The admin UI accepts and saves a host that raises 'invalid referer host' for every embed attempt from that origin, with no validation or UI feedback indicating the saved configuration is unmatchable by the enforcement path.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the format validation allows an optional port `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` hook strips only scheme and path (it does not remove `:port`). Meanwhile `record_for_host` parses the incoming referer/embed URL with `URI(host)` and compares against `uri.host`, which never includes the port. Therefore a persisted record like `example.com:3000` can pass validation and be saved, but `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?('http://example.com:3000/...')` will look for `example.com` and fail to match, causing embeds to be rejected as "invalid referer host" despite the admin configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same validation regex requires a dot and caps the TLD at five letters (\.[a-z]{2,5}), rejecting dotless hostnames and long TLDs (localhost, site.museum, blog.travel) that the previous free-text embeddable_hosts setting accepted and matched. A migrated row holding such a legacy value is displayed in the admin table but any edit-and-save of it fails the new format validation, so an admin who previously embedded from 'localhost' (dev setups) or a >5-letter TLD cannot re-save that host through the new UI at all.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host` with `/\A...\.[a-z]{2,5}...\Z/i`, which requires a dot and limits TLD length to 5 (e.g. rejects `localhost` and `site.museum`). The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` bulk-inserts legacy `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` rows via raw SQL, bypassing validations/callbacks, so such legacy values can exist in the DB and be displayed in the new admin UI. But when an admin later edits/saves via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, `host.save` will run the new validation and fail, making those legacy hosts unsavable through the UI. The previous `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` implementation performed URI/host comparisons without this regex restriction, so this is a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation and the migration creates no unique index on host, while record_for_host resolves duplicate rows via where(...).first, so the same hostname can be stored twice with different category_id values and the lookup silently picks the lowest-id row. An admin who adds the same host twice with different categories (nothing client- or server-side prevents it) gets every embedded topic for that host created in the older row's category regardless of the newer entry's intent, and nothing flags the conflicting configuration.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `EmbeddableHost` only has a format validation (`validates_format_of :host`) and the migration `create_embeddable_hosts` creates no unique index/constraint on `host`, so duplicate rows are allowed. Lookups use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that single returned row’s `category_id` to choose the category (`category: eh.try(:category_id)`). With duplicates (e.g., same host saved twice with different `category_id`), the behavior becomes incorrect/ambiguous and silently depends on which row `.first` returns, matching the finding’s concern. Nothing in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` prevents duplicates either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] belongs_to :category has no presence validation and nothing re-points or nullifies embeddable_hosts.category_id when a category is deleted — Discourse's category-deletion flow remaps topics but knows nothing about this new table, and there is no dependent option or destroy/reassign hook. Deleting a category that an allowlisted host references leaves a dangling category_id row; the next TopicEmbed.import for that host passes a nonexistent category to PostCreator and topic creation for that host fails with no surfaced error, silently killing feed embedding for that host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` rows with a required `category_id` (`db/migrate/...create_embeddable_hosts.rb` sets `null: false`; `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` always sets one), but there is no referential integrity (no FK) and no lifecycle handling for when a `Category` is deleted. `EmbeddableHost` only has `belongs_to :category` with no validation or reassignment/nullification hook (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`). Later, `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` as the `category:` argument to `PostCreator` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`), so a dangling `category_id` can be passed through after category deletion, plausibly breaking embed topic creation for that host. The diff contains no code to prevent or repair this dangling reference scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddingController#update persists nothing — it only re-renders the same OpenStruct built by fetch_embedding — and the client saveChanges action that calls embedding.update({}) is wired to no element in embedding.hbs, making the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route, the update action, and the client action inert dead code (the deletion test passes: removing the route in config/routes.rb, this action, and saveChanges removes the lying contract entirely). The shipped update route accepts and silently discards any payload, so a future developer who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action ships silent data loss believing the endpoint persists settings.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (new file) only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all`, with no mutation or persistence of any request params. Also, the client controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains no button or handler wired to `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and per-row save/delete via `embeddable-host`). So the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` route is currently inert/misleading. However, because nothing in this diff invokes the update path from the UI, this is more of a misleading/unused contract than a currently triggered correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec added for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance (verified: this file's single it-block checks Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController and no other spec in the diff references this controller), leaving the controller's entire behavior surface unverified — the blank-category_id-to-uncategorized defaulting, the render_json_error path for invalid hosts, and create/update/destroy request handling have zero assertions. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embedding controller spec likewise asserts only inheritance, so the load-path contract the new admin page depends on — EmbeddingSerializer emitting embeddable_host_ids plus an embeddable_hosts side-load array that the store's new plural _hydrateEmbedded branch consumes — is verified by no server spec anywhere in the diff (only the generic fruit/color fixtures in store-test exercise the hydration). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration reads site_settings rows with no guard for absence, so `execute(...WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'...)[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError on nil whenever no embed_category site_settings row exists — every fresh install and every site that never overrode that setting — aborting db:migrate before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can ever run. Fresh installs and all sites that never set embed_category fail db:migrate at this migration, blocking every upgrade containing this commit until the SQL is patched by hand.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim into the new table while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches `lower(host)` against the bare parsed hostname, so legacy entries stored as 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — forms the old feature's own specs explicitly supported — never match after the upgrade (the model's stripping only runs on save, and the migration bypasses the model). Upgraded sites whose admins entered scheme- or path-qualified hosts get 'invalid referer host' Discourse::InvalidAccess on every embedded comment page and rejected feed imports, silently, until an admin re-saves each row in the new UI.

[BUG] update feeds `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` — nil for a nonexistent id — straight into save_host, which executes `host.host = ...` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Saving an edit against a host another admin has just deleted (stale list) returns a 500 instead of a 404, showing the admin a server-error popup with no recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), so if the record doesn’t exist (e.g., stale UI editing a host that was deleted), `host` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy calls `host.destroy` on the result of `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check, raising NoMethodError when the id no longer exists. Two admins deleting the same host makes the second DELETE return a 500 instead of a 404, and because the component's `destroyRecord().then()` has no rejection handler the row silently stays in the admin list looking undeleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If the record is already deleted (e.g., two admins delete same host), `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a not-found response. On the client side, the component’s `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(...)`, so a failed DELETE won’t remove the row and (absent any global handler) won’t be handled locally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update renders the serialized embedding without applying any request params — the OpenStruct embedding has no editable fields — and no template in the diff invokes the frontend saveChanges action, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and the admin-embedding.js saveChanges/update({}) path are implementation work traceable to no requirement. Any client that PUTs /admin/customize/embedding receives a 200 success for a request that persisted nothing, and a future contributor who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action ships a control that silently does nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the fetched OpenStruct embedding (id + `embeddable_hosts`) without reading/applying any params, so a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` will succeed while persisting nothing (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). The frontend controller has a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`), but the new `embedding.hbs` template contains no control that triggers `saveChanges` (only addHost/deleteHost). This is diff-grounded as potentially misleading/dead implementation rather than a currently user-visible broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The per-request embed allow-list check changed from the in-memory cached SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, which runs an uncached `WHERE lower(host) = ?` query on every embed request, and the migration creates no index on host. Every embedded page's /embed/comments hit now costs a DB round trip (a scan, since a plain index would not serve lower()) — high-embed-traffic sites lose the previous zero-DB allow-list path and gain load proportional to embed views.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes embed allow-list validation from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` (in-memory setting string) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (called from `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, implying a DB query per request. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` without any index on `host`, and since the query wraps the column in `lower(host)`, a plain index wouldn’t help anyway without a functional index / normalized storage. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] before_validation strips the scheme and path but not the port while the format regex explicitly accepts `:[0-9]{1,5}`, and record_for_host compares the stored value against `uri.host` with the port removed, so a port-qualified host that validation and the UI accept can never match a referer. An admin who saves 'staging.example.com:8080' (accepted by the validation the diff itself added) gets 'invalid referer host' InvalidAccess for every embed from that origin, with the stored row permanently unmatchable until hand-edited.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `before_validation` strips only the scheme (`/^https?:\/\//`) and the path (`/\/.*$/`), leaving any `:port` intact, while the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer with `URI(host)` and then compares against `uri.host` (which excludes the port) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Therefore a saved value like `staging.example.com:8080` can pass validation and be persisted, but will never match `uri.host == "staging.example.com"`, causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false and embedding to fail with `invalid referer host`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost enforces only host format with no uniqueness validation and no unique index, while record_for_host resolves duplicates via `.first`, so two rows for the same host are accepted — including case variants, since the format regex is case-insensitive and the lookup lowercases. An admin who adds a case-variant duplicate and edits its category sees the edit accepted while embedded topics keep posting to the first row's category, with nothing indicating the edited row is dead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` without any uniqueness constraint: the model only has `validates_format_of :host` (no `validates_uniqueness_of`) and the migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with no unique index on `host`. Lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so duplicates (including case variants, since the regex is `/.../i` and the query lowercases) are accepted and resolved arbitrarily by `.first`. Since `TopicEmbed.import` selects category via `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and uses `category: eh.try(:category_id)`, an admin editing a duplicate row’s category could see saves succeed while embeds continue using the other row’s category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new belongs_to :category relationship registers no cleanup anywhere in the diff, so deleting a category that an embeddable host references leaves embeddable_hosts.category_id dangling. After an admin deletes a used category, TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator under skip_validations: true and creates topics pointing at a nonexistent category, and the admin UI renders that host row with a blank category via Discourse.Category.findById.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost with a required `category_id` (`db/migrate/...create_embeddable_hosts.rb` sets `null: false`; `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` has `belongs_to :category`) but adds no FK constraint, no `dependent` behavior, and no validation that the referenced category exists. If an admin deletes a category, existing `embeddable_hosts.category_id` can become dangling. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration interpolates each legacy embeddable_hosts setting line directly into an unescaped SQL string (execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"), so a single quote in any stored host line breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL during migration. An operator upgrading a site whose embeddable_hosts value contains a quote character — whether from a past admin entry, a site import, or a restored backup — has attacker-influenced SQL executed with full database privileges at deploy time; even a benign apostrophe aborts the migration and blocks the upgrade for the whole instance.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` comes from splitting the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (`val.split("\n")`) and is not escaped/quoted safely. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration copies each legacy embeddable_hosts setting line verbatim into the host column without the model's scheme/path stripping, while the new record_for_host requires an exact lower(host) = URI(...).host match, so migrated entries like 'https://example.com/1234' — a form the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported by URI-parsing each line — can never match after the upgrade. Operators whose embeddable_hosts contained scheme- or path-prefixed entries (exactly the 'https://example.com/1234' form the old code and its specs supported) silently lose those allowed hosts: every embed and topic-retriever request from them raises Discourse::InvalidAccess after upgrade, breaking the embedded comment sections on those external sites with no migration-time warning.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, legacy `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` lines are inserted via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without going through `EmbeddableHost` validations/callbacks. The model’s `before_validation` is what strips `http(s)://` and any path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). After upgrade, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which parses the referer/embed URL with `URI(...)` and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the migrated row contains a legacy value like `https://example.com/1234`, the stored `host` will be that full string, but the lookup key will be `example.com`, so it will never match. The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly supported scheme/path-prefixed entries by parsing each configured line via `URI(h).host`, so this is a regression that can break embedding for such previously-allowed hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update feeds EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first — nil for any nonexistent or already-deleted id — straight into save_host, whose `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The validation regex explicitly accepts port-bearing entries ((:[0-9]{1,5})?) but record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(...).host, which never contains a port, so a host saved with a port is an allowlist entry that can never match any referer. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] save_host persists any staff-supplied category_id with no check that the category exists or is not read-restricted, while the embed read path performs no category-permission check, so the new per-host category mapping can point embedding at a private category. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backfill guard `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is always false because cmd_tuples reports rows affected by DML and returns 0 for every SELECT result, so the INSERT at line 25 never executes while the unconditional `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` at line 31 destroys the old settings. Every site that upgrades with embedding configured ends up with an empty embeddable_hosts table and its whitelist and embed_category settings deleted: embed_controller immediately rejects every legitimate referer host, and the host list is permanently unrecoverable since no rows were migrated and the source rows are gone.

For the common Postgres `PG::Result`, `cmd_tuples` reports affected rows for DML and is 0/empty for `SELECT`, so this guard can prevent the backfill from ever running even when the `site_settings` row exists. The migration then unconditionally executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would drop the old configuration while inserting no `embeddable_hosts` rows, leaving the whitelist empty and causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` checks (e.g., in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`) to reject legitimate embeds after upgrade.

WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError on nil when the query returns no row — the common case, since site_settings stores only overrides and most sites (and every fresh install, which has no embed_category row at all) return an empty result — and the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback at line 14 is unreachable dead code because line 11 crashes before the fallback can run. `rake db:migrate` aborts with NoMethodError on fresh installs and on any production site that never set embed_category (or whose embed_category value no longer matches a category name), blocking the entire deploy.

If the query returns 0 rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row for `embed_category`, or value doesn’t match any category name), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, directly interpolating the old `site_settings` string into SQL and bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization (scheme/path stripping) and its format validation (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings rows inside a `change` migration with no inverse, no down path, and no backup/export step, making the destructive data move irreversible. `rake db:rollback` after this migration drops the embeddable_hosts table and leaves the deleted settings unrestored, so operators who need to back out a bad release lose the embedding configuration in both the forward and backward directions.

An admin who deletes a category that embeddable hosts post to leaves dangling rows: the admin UI renders a blank category badge and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator, so new embeds for that host break or land in an invalid category.
